00290bb7079d83ef.description: ORAC Gallery is developing a focused, curated presentation for its official Booth #2102 at Spectrum Chicago 2026. Rather than creating a crowded group display, the gallery intends to build a visually coherent presentation in which each selected work has a clear presence within the approximately 200 sq. ft. booth. We are particularly interested in artists with a distinctive and recognisable visual language, a consistent professional practice and a body of work that can function strongly within an international art-fair context. There is no fixed theme or required medium. Applications will be considered in relation to artistic quality, conceptual clarity, coherence of the proposed works, scale, physical presence, pricing, logistical feasibility and the potential dialogue between the works included in the final presentation. Artists are encouraged to submit a carefully edited group of works that genuinely represents the current direction of their practice rather than a broad overview of unrelated projects. The open call also forms part of ORAC Gallery's wider international artist research, with particular interest in practices that may develop into a longer-term curatorial dialogue with the gallery.
00290bb7079d83ef.title: Open Call for Artists - Spectrum Chicago 2026 | ORAC Gallery

Winners revealed during Art Basel Miami on December 3, 2026. Judged by a 10-member international jury including leading voices in contemporary art and culture. Learn more → award.art SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Every submission must link to the following three core elements. These requirements apply equally to standalone websites and social media profiles linked via a .ART domain. A. Artist Identity Biography (min 100 words) describing who the artist or collective is, their practice, and background Links to social media or external portfolio (optional but encouraged) B. Artwork Presentation High-quality images, video, or 3D models of the work Concise descriptions or captions for each piece Technical details: medium and materials used, dimensions, and software or digital tools (if applicable) Optional: embedded media or additional documentation (sound, video, animations) C. Narrative - The Story Behind the Work Each submission must include one of the following: A written text, or a link to it (min 100 words) describing the artwork's creation, materials, inspiration, and concept A video (30 secs) with the artist or collective member(s) speaking directly about the work and its process The narrative should reflect: The concept and inspiration behind the work The narrative of creation - how the work came to be Any personal or cultural contexts that shaped the work

05757e8d2df17a86.description: Located underneath L'Objet Trouvé in Prague, FOUND OBJECT is a recently opened art space dedicated to experimental, process-based, and cross-disciplinary artistic practices. Following a summer break, the group exhibition **_Works in Progress_** will mark the reopening of the space and act as an introduction to its curatorial direction: open, playful, research-led, and attentive to artistic processes as much as to final outcomes. For this exhibition, we are looking for projects that approach the artwork not as a final, fixed object, but as a creature, system or entity that unfolds over time: through research, interaction, collaboration, repetition, failure, play, or transformation. We welcome works that are literally unfinished, ongoing, or still evolving, as well as finalized projects that reveal the process behind their making. The exhibition can also be an opportunity for artists to present their work in a different way - by sharing sketches, research material, documentation, trials, fragments, or unfinished stages that would be otherwise left unseen. We are especially interested in works that are interactive and/or playful, social, research-based, experimental. All media are welcome, with a particular interest in installation, low-tech interactive experiments, documentary practices and participatory formats. Artists are encouraged, but not required, to continue developing or activating the work during the exhibition.
05757e8d2df17a86.title: WORKS IN PROGRESS

067d3022c4550c5a.description: The Elevated Spaces Residency is a bi-annual offering of time and space at our property in the redwoods of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Artists will have privacy of our land and cabin, entirely to themselves, to pursue their projects. The cabin is basic. Similar in size and supply to an alpine mountain hut. There's solar/battery power, but not much of it. Outside, there's a comfortable outhouse, a heated outdoor shower, and a small A-frame that can be used as a studio. It's not quite camping, but not far removed from it-with few distractions, just enough creature comforts, and ample nature to inspire. Town is a 15 minute drive down the hill and artists will need to have a car to access and resupply their stay. You can find more details and a brief tour of the property here. The land is 10 acres of steep and thickly wooded redwood, oak, madrone, and fir. The area holding our cabin, and associated structures and paths, encompasses about 2 acres. We are offering a two week block of time to artists, the exact time of which is negotiable depending on the project and artist's needs. While there is no specific guidance on the types of art and exploration we hope artists might pursue, when detailing what you've done in the past, and what you plan to create, applicants should also answer the question: "Why here?"

0fa3503fcb45301d.description: Artists and writers of international, national and Texas origin are invited to apply for two-month, funded studio residencies to produce work in rare scale and focus, with generous support and immersive space, in an historic setting fifty miles south of Dallas, Texas. Residents are hosted at 100 West - a vast, two-story former Odd Fellows lodge, virtually unaltered since its 1890s construction, preserved and minimally furnished with pieces designed and built from the first-floor wood shop. Private artist studios are 2,400 square-feet; writing studio is 600 square-feet; kitchen and dining room are shared. Studio work is prioritized and complemented by introductions to professional networks and world-class institutions in North Texas. This residency takes place in downtown Corsicana - the birthplace of the Texas oil industry and the intersection of this country's cultural and geographic South and West. Oil booms in the 1890s and 1920s produced an exuberant setting, which declined in care and use by the late 20th century before reviving in the last decade. The complex story of rural and small-town America contributes generative context to this residency experience and consequentially enriches contemporary art and literature. **2-Month Terms:** 2 Artists and 1 Writer hosted each term: * WINTER: January 4 - February 23 * SPRING: March 1 - April 27 * FALL: October 11 - December 7 **Expectations of Residents:** * Studio focus and productivity is the first priority; social programming is second. * Self-directed and self-sufficient without need for studio production help. Occasional support is available. * PRESENTATION: second Thursday of residency: 20-minutes, Artists project image / video / slideshow of past work. Writers deliver readings. * OPEN STUDIOS: last Saturday of residency from 12 - 4 PM.
0fa3503fcb45301d.restrictions: other: International, United States, and Texas-based eligibility. Sound-based work is generally not hosted. Performance, composition and sound-based applicants should inquire before applying by contacting residency director to ensure the residency can support their practice successfully. Ceramic, fiberglass and aerosol-based work not accommodated.
0fa3503fcb45301d.title: 2-Month Funded Artist & Writer Residency

12e2053de543c624.description: Sintra, Portugal | October 24 - November 1, 2026 A 7-day immersive training for practitioners working with voice, body, movement, or creativity. Developed by Kate Smith, The Embodied Voice integrates voice, movement, and improvisation as pathways to presence, expression, and embodied awareness. This intimate program (limited to 10 participants) offers a deep dive into the principles and methodology behind the practice, focusing on experiential learning and embodied inquiry. Rather than a certification, the training supports participants in deepening their own practice and expanding their capacity to facilitate creative and relational processes. The training is structured around four core pillars: Somatics & the Singing Body, Expressive Voice, Vocal Improvisation, and Leadership & Facilitation. Participants will explore body-voice integration, nervous system awareness, emotional expression, improvisation as a creative and relational tool, and embodied leadership in non-hierarchical learning environments. The program includes online preparation (course + orientation calls), 7 days of in-person training, and a post-training integration session. The training takes place in Sintra, Portugal, a unique setting known for its lush forests, historical sites, and tranquil atmosphere. 18b99ce3eb90fc70.description: For our second exhibition, we invite artists to engage with the theme of "Bubble." Bubbles can be safe spaces, but they can also create boundaries. Both online and in real life, we often move within our own circles, surrounded by people, information, and perspectives that reinforce our existing views. What do we see when we only see what we want to see? Are our bubbles a form of protection or a limitation? And what happens when we try to leave them? Do we even want to step outside them? We are looking for artistic works that explore the theme from personal, social, political, digital, or entirely individual perspectives. Both existing works and new works are welcome. The Open Call is international. No matter where you are based, you are welcome to apply.

The theme for the Yonge + St Clair neighbourhood this year is: Intersections. Yonge + St. Clair has long been a place where people, ideas and city life intersect. Situated between downtown and uptown Toronto, the neighbourhood brings together residents, businesses, office workers and visitors while continuing to evolve through significant growth and investment. These intersections between communities, disciplines, history, and progress shape the identity of the neighbourhood and the experiences of those who move through it each day. Artists are invited to interpret Intersections through their own creative and critical lens. Proposals may explore themes of convergence, transformation, movement, identity, exchange, and/or the evolving relationship between people and place. The theme is intentionally broad, encouraging innovative responses that activate the selected site. **Duration** 10 days • January 22 - January 31, 2027 **Timeline** September 13, 2026, Submission deadline Late September 2026, Artists selected October 2026, Final project information submitted to DesignTO November 2026, DesignTO Festival announcement January 14-21, 2027, Installation period January 22-31, 2027, Exhibition February 1-2, 2027, De-installation (unless exhibit extended)

GLEAN taps into the creativity of artists to inspire people to think about their consumption habits, the waste they generate, and the resources they throw away. **We reserve one residency position for a student currently enrolled in an art program at a local college or university.** Student applications will be considered separately from other artist applications. GLEAN seeks to hear from artists with a broad range of experiences and perspectives from the many communities in the Portland area. We encourage artists working in a variety of media to apply. You can learn more about past GLEAN artists [**on our website.**](https://www.gleanportland.com/) GLEAN is a partnership between [**Recology**](https://www.recology.com/recology-portland/), an employee-owned integrated resource recovery and recycling company; [**Metro**](https://www.oregonmetro.gov/), the regional government that manages the Portland area's garbage and recycling system; and [**ReClaim It**](https://www.reclaimitpdx.org/), an environmental arts non-profit.

1ca3cb59320cc18b.description: Could dreams and nightmares be the potent driving force behind our creative processes, the mysterious catalysts igniting the flame of artistic inspiration? A significant number of artists affirm this belief wholeheartedly. Some find their deepest inspirations enveloped in the essence of dreams, immersing themselves in a blissful trance of creation. This state transcends mere aspiration, becoming a surreal canvas where possibilities bloom endlessly, a place where the mind wanders, seeking the sublime, the ethereal, fostering an insatiable quest to reach heights previously unimagined, somehow, somewhere. On the flip side, many others journey through the chilling domains of nightmares, a voyage marked by relentless internal conflicts and cold sweats that pierce the stillness of the night. These artists find themselves wrestling with the darker fragments of their psyche, exploring into corners where fears manifest and insecurities gnaw persistently. It's a place where conflict brews, giving birth to creations steeped in raw, unfiltered emotion, art that doesn't shy away from exposing the tumultuous storms raging within. It serves as both an exploration and an exorcism of the deep-seated darkness that resides in the corners of the human spirit. Here, the beauty arises from the conflict, the chaos, offering a catharsis that is both profound and unsettling. "I know, I've been there, I am still." This exhibition aims to unearth the profound connections between the subconscious dream world and the pulsating, sometimes harrowing heartbeat of artistic creation, offering a sanctuary for reflection, resonance, and perhaps, revelation. Gallery Space Our gallery is located in one of the most iconic and visited areas in the world- the Tower Bridge district of London. Situated on Tooley Street, the historic link between London Bridge and Tower Bridge, we are just two minutes from both landmarks, four minutes from The Shard, and six minutes from the Tower of London, home to the Royal Crown Jewels. With over 5 million people passing through Tooley Street each month, our gallery has become a celebrated destination. Also- "Our gallery is proud to be one of the 4,000 blue-chip galleries listed on Artsy." Submission Guidelines To apply, email us three images of your work (three different pieces), each with its title, size in cm, medium, price, and a short biography of no more than 150 words. Email submissions should be sent to [boomergallery@gmail.com](mailto:boomergallery@gmail.com). Eligible media include, but are not limited to, paintings, sculptures, photography, installations, prints, textiles, illustrations, digital art, Ai assisted art, poems, etc. Application is free, but a £189 fee (including VAT) applies for each selected artist. This fee covers an extensive suite of benefits: • Printed posters and brochures • Admin support • Graphic designer services • Champagne & caviar at the opening event • Professional photographer to document the event • Hostess, security, and bartender services at the opening • Printing and framing for the artists who opt for that (printing and framing is included in the price). Our exhibition catalogs are state-of-the-art. They present the artist's profile in a magazine-like format, making them valuable beyond the exhibition itself. The catalog will be permanently displayed on our website and continuously circulated by artists, art collectors, and enthusiasts. We facilitate direct connections between artists and collectors and do not charge a commission. Each sale happens directly between the artist and the customer. If you would like us to broker the sale, a 20% VAT will be applied on top of your initial price so please take that into consideration when pricing your works. Printing and Framing Support: If you're an accepted artist facing difficulties shipping your work to us, you can send us photos of your work. We'll print and frame them for you at no additional cost. Rest assured, we strive to match the quality of your original artwork as closely as possible. Frame sizes available: 1\. 32 x 32 cm 2\. 30 x 40 cm A frequent question we receive is: how much should I price my prints if I decide to go with that option? We typically price a framed print at £400, but if you have a different price in mind, please let us know. Remember, printing and framing are included in the participation fee, you don't have to pay anything extra. Important dates: \* Application deadline: 2nd September 2026 \* Artwork delivery date: 10th September 2026 \* Exhibition days: from 11th to the 16th September 2026 \* Opening event on 11th September, from 6:00 to 9:00 pm Event: This is a physical exhibition taking place in our iconic gallery space in the Tower Bridge district, London. Beverages at the event: Champagne, Cocktails, and Caviar. Moreover, we are pleased to permanently include you in our Advisory Program. This program allows us to connect our clients with both emerging and established artists, tailored to their individual preferences, budgets, and styles. By understanding our clients' unique needs, we guide them toward artists whose work aligns with their vision. Since all our exhibitions are thematically curated, and we meticulously catalog every artist we work with, the process of matching clients with the right artists becomes seamless and efficient. If you would like to explore our past exhibitions or browse the works of other artists featured in our catalogs, please visit our website and check the advisory section. Important: When applying, please include "D&M" in the subject line of your email. Good luck to all entrants!
1ca3cb59320cc18b.title: Dreams & Nightmares - Call for Artists

3555b38c1d5ccb6e.description: The Eleanor D. Wilson Museum at Hollins University invites artists and craftspeople to submit work for a planned publication and an upcoming group exhibition (Fall 2028) celebrating the evolving landscape of contemporary craft in the Appalachian region. At the close of the exhibition, three artworks will be chosen by the Hollins community to be acquired by the museum for its permanent collection. In Belonging: A Culture of Place, bell hooks explores the meaning of home through her return to Kentucky after years away. At the end of the preface, hooks notes that the collection pays "tribute to the past as a resource that can serve as a foundation for us to revision and renew our commitment to the present, to making a world where all people can live fully and well; where everyone can belong." Our exhibition, Belonging: Contemporary Appalachian Craft (working title) asks: What does it mean for regional artists and craftspeople to create contemporary works that respond to current issues while remaining firmly rooted in history and tradition? We are also interested in understanding what "Appalachia" means to artists from or living in the region. Is it a place, a people, a history or culture? And how does their work speak to this idea while creating a shared space of belonging? We are seeking work that balances tradition and pride of place with contemporary concerns, such as ecological impact or identity politics. We strongly encourage applications from traditionally marginalized communities, including women, LGBTQIA+, BIPOC, disabled, and Indigenous artists. Open to artists from and/or currently living and working within the defined Appalachian region of: Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Maryland, Mississippi, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia Artist must be at least 18 years of age All submitted artworks must be entirely original in concept and creation (not from a kit or class project)
3555b38c1d5ccb6e.organisation: Eleanor D. Wilson Museum, Hollins University
rewards: Exhibition and/or publication opportunity and 3 works will be acquired by the museum

35d4457880da0dbe.description: In October 2026, London Art Collective will present ArtEvol 2026: A View from Everywhere, a large-scale international group exhibition bringing together artists working across different cultures, disciplines and lived realities. Through an international Open Call, the exhibition seeks works that reveal how differently the same world can be seen, understood and represented. The title begins with a simple contradiction: no one can see from everywhere. Every perspective is shaped by where we stand, what we have experienced and the structures through which we encounter the world. Rather than searching for a single, universal point of view, the exhibition places different positions alongside one another. Some may overlap; others may disagree or remain unresolved. Together, they form a view that belongs to no single person or place. The exhibition will be presented through a salon-style display within the white cube. Works will appear in close proximity, creating unexpected connections across geography, medium and subject. Painting, sculpture, installation, photography, moving image, digital media and interdisciplinary practices are all welcome. The aim is not to flatten these differences into a shared message, but to allow each work to retain its own position while becoming part of a wider conversation. Curated by Nelson Qin and organised by London Art Collective (LAC), A View from Everywhere will be selected by an international jury of curators, artists, critics and scholars. The jury will consider the clarity of each artist's practice, the strength of the work and what it brings to the exhibition as a whole. The exhibition does not set out to offer a complete picture of the world. Instead, it asks what might become visible when many partial views are brought together.
35d4457880da0dbe.restrictions: other: * Applicants must be 18 years of age or older by the application deadline. * We welcome submissions from individual artists and collectives of all nationalities. We encourage diverse voices and practices across all disciplines and geographies. * Artworks can be existing pieces, but we encourage you to submit new artworks. * We understand some artists may face barriers to participation due to factors such as disability, gender, age, or ethnic background. London Art Collective welcomes applications from all artists and especially encourages those from marginalised communities.

3a1e824d3e959feb.description: **_Where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?_** ​spazioSERRA will turn ten in 2027. That's long enough to see a shift in perspective. In recent years, cities have changed, as have the ways of experiencing public spaces, the timeframe of relationships and cultural production. The way art is viewed and the way artists are asked to exist in the present have also changed. And in the meantime, we've changed too. Not only in the way we observe, imagine, and curate, but first and foremost, as people. spazioSERRA was born as a place open to experimentation, and we've grown alongside it. But over time, we've begun to wonder if some of the mechanisms of independent art haven't slowly come to resemble what they were trying to distance themselves from. The deadlines, the need to arrive with already defined ideas, the need to know everything before even starting. We asked ourselves how many possibilities remain when an artistic practice must become immediately exhibitable, performable, and producible. How many attempts disappear because they don't yet have a defined form. And how many ideas, instead, require time, doubt, and error. This is why the 2026 open call for artists was born from a different desire. We're not looking for finished projects. We're not looking for established visions. We'd like to explore practices. Processes. Obsessions. Still-unresolved questions. We're interested in understanding your imprints, what informs your research, what tensions drive it, what possibilities it opens and contradicts within the contemporary scene. Site-specific installations, performances, editorial productions, videos, urban interventions, hybrid collaborations, or still-formless forms: the point is not the format, but the urgency that permeates it. We hope this open call will be the beginning of a space geared toward future projects, open to anyone willing to engage with shared research that can still slow down, change direction, and remain incomplete long enough to transform itself. Because perhaps today the most radical action for a public space dedicated to contemporary art is not to reflect immediacy, but to have the courage to support a still uncertain process.
3a1e824d3e959feb.fee_note: 12 EUR - participation is subject to the payment of a spazioSERRA 2026-2027 membership fee
3a1e824d3e959feb.title: Where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?

3e3555fd90d38a04.description: Algae, fungi, yeast, natural fibres... grown materials are substances cultivated with living organisms, rather than being extracted from the earth. They are natural, renewable, and biodegradable, whether grown in a lab or on land. The UK's bioeconomy is a government growth priority: the [2025 Modern Industrial Strategy](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/the-uks-modern-industrial-strategy-2025) names engineering biology as one of six frontier industries, with an ambition for global leadership by 2030. Globally, [the market for mycelium-based materials](https://www.gminsights.com/industry-analysis/mycelium-market) alone is projected to grow from around $3.6 billion today to over $5 billion by 2030, as fashion, construction and packaging industries look for alternatives to plastic, leather and other petrochemical- and animal-derived materials. Yet the UK's own living landscapes for grown materials are themselves under threat. [Seagrass meadows on the west coast of Wales](https://www.projectseagrass.org/blogs/restoring-our-damaged-seagrass-meadows/) have depleted by 92% over the last century, while only around 30,000 hectares remain of Scotland's [temperate rainforests](https://savingscotlandsrainforest.org.uk/). The UK's grown ecosystems are as fragile as they are abundant. **Design Researchers in Residence** is open to designers and researchers from disciplines including but not limited to: biodesign, fashion and textiles, industrial design, architecture, systems and policy research, material innovation, craft or graphic design. We are interested in research that spans the handmade and tactile to the biofabricated and engineered, embedded in natural intelligence. This includes Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK), biodesign and biofabrication practices that work with living systems.
3e3555fd90d38a04.restrictions: other: **Design Researchers in Residence: Grown** programme will run from October 2026 to June 2027. The accompanying residency display will be open from June 2027 to September 2027. To be eligible, residents must live and work in the UK, have graduated or set up a design-related business within the last five years, and must have demonstrable experience in carrying out independent research.
3e3555fd90d38a04.title: Design Researchers in Residence

3ed4f87826e9ffe9.description: Public Art Agency Sweden, now a part of Moderna Museet (Museum of Modern Art), is announcing a new opportunity for artists to submit sketch proposals. The new commission concerns a permanent artwork in the Admiralty House's outdoor environment on Skeppsholmen. A collaboration between Public Art Agency Sweden and the National Property Board of Sweden. Skeppsholmen is located in the middle of Stockholm's inlet and is one of the city's most visited places. As part of the National Urban Park, the environment is protected for its significant cultural-historical values. The Admiralty House was built for the Navy's Board of Directors and was completed in 1650. Since its inception, the building has both changed its appearance and served various purposes such as the National Archives, grain warehouses, barracks and offices. In connection with the reconstruction of the Admiralty House and adaptation for the Swedish Institute of International Affairs, a commission is announced for an outdoor public art project. The curatorial vision focuses on Skeppsholmen as a historical landscape shaped by its various connections to the outside world. A place where human movements have manifested themselves in park environments, building history and contemporary cultural exchanges. Through the new artwork, the island's diversity of public art is complemented by a contemporary work that becomes yet another layer of time in the island's history. Skeppsholmen will be given a new landmark with possible locations on both the north and south sides of the Admiralty House.
3ed4f87826e9ffe9.title: Call for Sketch Proposals for Skeppsholmen

3f9bcb6e2c21966e.description: The National Gallery of Iceland is proud to announce an artist residency open call in relation to its CUSP program, a European cooperation project funded through Creative Europe's Culture grant. This is the first of four residency stays offered to different artists through the program, one in each of the five participating countries; Iceland, Norway, Czechia and Ukraine, to be followed by two micro residencies in the Netherlands and Iceland. This residency programme brings together artists working time based media and museum professionals, conservators, and technology specialists working to develop the preservation and conservation methodologies required to ensure the long-term endurance of artworks. The artist will meet with a preservation specialist or conservator specializing in time based media art who will conduct an in-depth artist interview aimed at addressing the preservation needs of the medium in which the artist works. The artist will be required to present publicly their body of work and working methods during an open-lab masterclass to be designed in collaboration with the museum.

4158806b312a67e3.description: Prisma Estúdio is a nonprofit volunteer-run cultural association in the most diverse quarter of central Lisbon. Dedicated to the research, creation, and dissemination of the arts, our mission is to support emerging artists from various creative backgrounds and helping them to develop their practice and share their work. Drawing on the principles of research, creation, production, distribution and promotion of artistic and cultural events, we support the arts to the benefit of our local and international community. Since 2019, our studio has been supporting artists from a diverse range of creative practices. We gained association status in February 2020 and have since collaborated with hundreds of artists - hosting exhibitions, salons, concerts, workshops, poetry slams and arts & craft fairs. We have created a space where our members consistently return to find inspiration and make connections. This gives a foundation for the residency program to build upon, bringing together likeminded locals and internationals alike. __ You will be immersed in Lisbon's vibrant underground artistic community. Engage in our eclectic program of events, schedule of workshops, while collaborating with community members. We offer residents the possibility to explore techniques, concepts, ideas, and collaborations, and to develop any project either specific to the residency or ongoing. Throughout, you will receive friendly guidance and peer-to-peer support from our welcoming community and the Prisma AiR team. 1-1 consultations with artist members of the team can be requested. The residents will have the opportunity to get to know Lisbon's art scene through gallery visits, exhibition openings, talks and open studio visits. During the last week of the program we give our residents full autonomy to take over the space, be it through a final showcase of works, talks, workshop, open studio, or performance in the Prisma space.
4158806b312a67e3.title: Prisma Estúdio Residency Open Call

4846c387f3dead1a.description: The Napa Lighted Art Festival is a celebration of creative arts, technology, and lights. The Napa Lighted Art Festival is a free, open-air festival with the nighttime backdrop of downtown Napa. It is open to all members of the public and will attract admirers from near and far. Currently in its 8th edition, the festival supports innovative techniques using light and light technologies as a growing art medium. Both artists and artist groups are encouraged to apply to have an installation featured at the Napa Lighted Art Festival. For the 2026 Festival, the curatorial team will select approximately 10 installations to receive a stipend between $2,000-$10,000. Artists interested in submitting should consider both the audience and the outdoor environment of the festival when proposing a project. Each artwork of the Napa Lighted Art Festival will be open and operational for all festival hours for each of the nights. The spirit of the Napa Lighted Art Festival embodies the following core concepts: * Innovative * Contemporary * Uplifting * Inspiring * Imaginative The festival supports innovative techniques using light and light technologies as a growing art medium. **Light itself in any form should be the actual artwork, and we require that the role of light be essential to your concept.** We are not looking for artworks where light is used only to illuminate it. We also strongly encourage new technologies and innovative use of light. As well as new ideas for artworks, we are open to receiving proposals to exhibit existing works, provided they meet the festival themes and criteria. Artwork could include any of the following genres and/or technology: light sculptures, light art, video art, 3D video mapping projections, LED, fiber optics, custom gobo designs, interactive works, lasers etc. **General Festival Information** _Festival Dates:_ January 17th - February 15th, 2026 _Festival Times:_ Sunday-Thursday 6:00-9:00 p.m. and Friday-Saturday 6:00-10:00 p.m. _Location:_ Various sites and buildings in the Napa Downtown Area **Napa Lighted Art Festival** The Napa Lighted Art Festival started in 2017 and the festival had the 7th exhibition in 2025. The festival's attendance is approximately 70,000. In addition to the art installations, past festivals have included the iconic Napa Valley hot air balloons called "Night Bloom" that lit up the Oxbow Commons and a community driven Lantern Parade where everyone gets to make their own lighted art. The festival has included artist meet and greet experiences, educational or historical tours, and musical performances. The festival is free and open to the public. **Artwork Selection Criteria** **_Construction_**_:_ All works at Napa Lighted Art Festival are staged in the public spaces for an extended time and this requires rigid constructions. At times, the weather in Napa during the winter can vary from year to year. Napa can be stormy, wet and cold, so the technical feasibility, rigidity and durability of your concept is of utmost importance. A construction overview of durability is required with your submission. For some structures or sculptures, it will be required to provide stamped engineering drawings. **_Sound_**_:_ The use of sound is encouraged when possible with projection mapping pieces. The soundtrack should be submitted with the correlating visuals. **_Lighting:_** All sculptures or physical artwork must be able to be powered the entire time or provide a timer to self-turn-on every evening by 6pm. The festival staff will not manually turn on any installation. **_Period_**_:_ Digital artwork must be available and uploaded to the provide Drop Box folder by Monday December 8, 2025. Sculptures or any physical art for the festival needs to arrive and be installed no later than January 10, 2026 (and deinstalled no later than February 28, 2026). **_Visitor Experience_**_:_ Please keep in mind that your work may be positioned in pedestrian zones, sidewalks, parking lots, or perhaps in a plaza or park-like setting. Visitors will be able to experience your artwork from approximately 50-100 feet for installations such as projection artwork on buildings or be able to touch it for physical artwork. They will expect to be amazed as they walk from exhibit to exhibit but also spend time at each installation. Community members and visitors should enjoy sharing their experience with others and/or have a deeper personal understanding about the relationship between light, art and the festival's core concepts & theme. **_Location_**_:_ There are different types of locations along the festival art walk route. Your work will be positioned in a pedestrian zone adjacent to a private or public building, mainly along the downtown corridor. The potential locations are included but are subject to change. The artist may suggest a location for the artwork upon submission; however, the curatorial team will make the final decision in favor of the entire visitor experience of the festival route. **_Technical Limitations_**_:_ The artist will be provided with a description of the technical limitations for each site. The festival strives to push the boundaries of technology through art. However, the safety and well-being of the participants and property are of the highest importance. Please note there are safety considerations as people will be moving through and around the art installation. There may be limitations due to building code and other factors. Therefore, based on budget and physical location, there may be limitations to achieve technical realization. In some cases, a different approach may be needed or recommended in consultation with the artist. **_Curatorial Team:_** Curatorial team consisting of City of Napa staff and possible consultants conducting the initial review of the submissions to ensure the applications are complete as well as meet the artistic and technical requirements For installations at private property sites, the property owners often are involved in the final selection of the installations. The curatorial team will select artworks that together form a coherent and harmonious exhibition based upon the goals and core concepts for the festival.

The curatorial team will then review the artworks for the festival based on both the artistic impact of the work, the creativity of the concept, and the alignment with the festival's core concepts and selection criteria list below. 50e8a467f13ae175.description: On August 2, 2027, the longest total solar eclipse visible from land in the twenty-first century will pass directly over Luxor, Egypt, reaching more than six minutes of totality above one of the most historically and symbolically significant landscapes on Earth. The Luxor Eclipse Residency is an artist-run residency, creative expedition, and archival project bringing together six participants for 10 nights and 11 days in the heart of ancient Thebes. Residents will stay in a private home with a walled garden less than two miles from the Valley of the Kings, where generations of rulers were entombed within a landscape designed around ideas of death, rebirth, resurrection, and the eternal journey of the soul. The residency is organized around the concept of Akhet-the Egyptian horizon where heaven and earth meet, where the visible and invisible touch, and where transformation becomes possible. Applicants are invited to explore questions surrounding memory, mythology, consciousness, dreamwork, ancestral connection, reincarnation, divine feminine and masculine cycles, and humanity's relationship to the cosmos. Rather than prescribing a single interpretation, the residency welcomes diverse perspectives on what an eclipse over the Valley of the Kings might symbolize for our present moment. Participants are encouraged to develop between one and six works initiated during or inspired by the residency experience. Selected works will be included in a virtual exhibition and archival collection dedicated to documenting artistic responses to one of the rarest astronomical events of our lifetime. Residency amenities include lodging, ground transportation, scheduled (but not mandatory) group visits to major archaeological sites, Sunday dinners, delivered drinking water, and a welcome package containing eclipse-viewing supplies and other creative materials. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until all six places have been filled for July 30, 2027 - August 9, 2027.
50e8a467f13ae175.title: Luxor Eclipse Residency 2027

58ba9cb184dbe93e.description: The Open Arts Residency Programme is a structured platform designed to support artists, writers, curators, and cultural practitioners seeking time, space, and community to develop their work. To ensure accessibility and sustainability, the residency programme operates through two structured pathways: you can apply for the self-funded residency and short-term fully funded residency for artists in need. The Open Arts Self-Funded Residency is designed for artists and cultural practitioners who are able to support their participation independently or through external sponsorship, academic funding, or institutional grants. This residency provides a self-directed creative environment, allowing residents to focus on research, writing, artistic production, or project development. Residency Period Self-funded residencies are offered annually between january and December, when the Open Arts Space is fully operational for resident engagement and programming. Fully Funded Short-Stay Residency Open Arts offers a limited number of fully funded short-stay residencies for artists who demonstrate exceptional artistic potential but lack the financial means to participate in long term stays. 6b87730045d4b0cf.description: Could dreams and nightmares be the potent driving force behind our creative processes, the mysterious catalysts igniting the flame of artistic inspiration? A significant number of artists affirm this belief wholeheartedly. Some find their deepest inspirations enveloped in the essence of dreams, immersing themselves in a blissful trance of creation. This state transcends mere aspiration, becoming a surreal canvas where possibilities bloom endlessly, a place where the mind wanders, seeking the sublime, the ethereal, fostering an insatiable quest to reach heights previously unimagined, somehow, somewhere. On the flip side, many others journey through the chilling domains of nightmares, a voyage marked by relentless internal conflicts and cold sweats that pierce the stillness of the night. These artists find themselves wrestling with the darker fragments of their psyche, exploring into corners where fears manifest and insecurities gnaw persistently. It's a place where conflict brews, giving birth to creations steeped in raw, unfiltered emotion, art that doesn't shy away from exposing the tumultuous storms raging within. It serves as both an exploration and an exorcism of the deep-seated darkness that resides in the corners of the human spirit. Here, the beauty arises from the conflict, the chaos, offering a catharsis that is both profound and unsettling. "I know, I've been there, I am still." This exhibition aims to unearth the profound connections between the subconscious dream world and the pulsating, sometimes harrowing heartbeat of artistic creation, offering a sanctuary for reflection, resonance, and perhaps, revelation. Gallery Space Our gallery is located in one of the most iconic and visited areas in the world- the Tower Bridge district of London.
6b87730045d4b0cf.title: Dreams & Nightmares - Call for Artists: Exhibit Your Art at a Landmark Central London Gallery

6ecb52b92a2f63c8.description: This residency is an opportunity for international artists to stay and work in Lisbon for one to three months during the time period of May 01, 2026 - December 22, 2026. The Euroatla residency is an independent artist space meant for self-sufficient artists looking for a place of reflection away from their usual environment. Euroatla has two formats of residency to choose from. The first is an independent residency solely based at Euroatla while the other is done in partnership with Hangar, which includes an open day and curatorial support. Outside of ordinary constraints such as day jobs, commissions and exhibition deadlines, residencies offer artists the time, space and resources to experiment with their work and try new approaches. By connecting with Lisbon's art scene and being in a new context artists can take away new ideas and viewpoints that will benefit the development of their practice. Euroatla provides a private self-contained living and working space located in a building with another studio that is used by Portuguese artists. We can accommodate one international artist at the time, with the maximum capacity of two people. We are open to emerging and established artists from all disciplines within the visual arts. It is also open to researchers, writers, musicians, curators and cultural programmers. Applications must include a CV (max 700 words), a project proposal (including specifics for how you plan to use your time in this residency), an artist statement (a general statement about your work and brief explanation of your submitted images or text, max 250 words), and a portfolio in a single PDF file. The application process is free. The residency fee is €1,500 per month. Participants are selected through an open call and jury process, with results communicated via email within one week. For further information, please contact: euroatlaresidencies@gmail.com
6ecb52b92a2f63c8.title: Spring RESIDENCY in LISBON _ EUROATLA Residency

Through weekly online sessions, it brings together a diverse group of participants to engage in critical dialogue, present their work, exchange methods and ideas, and foster reflective practice. The program culminates in in-person gatherings, with the first two taking place at Bled Contemporary Music Week [June 22-26, 2026, January 11-15, 2027]. - FORMAT: Weekly online sessions via Zoom (Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, 90 minutes) FOR: Composers, performers, musicologists, researchers, pedagogues, producers, and other practitioners engaged in the field of music and art, at any stage of their academic or artistic development. Applications are welcome from both emerging and established practitioners; no specific subfield or specialization is required. The New Symposium is a weekly online residency program that builds an international community of music practitioners, theorists, and researchers. Meeting every Saturday on Zoom, participants present their work, share research questions, and engage in peer-led discussions that emphasize critical reflection and the practice of critical dialogue. Each session offers an open space for ideas, where diverse perspectives meet and participants are encouraged to question, challenge, and expand their approaches. The program culminates in an in-person gatherings, the first upcoming meeting will be at Bled Contemporary Music Week, where the working group meets on location, continues its research activities, and takes part in the festival concerts, symposia, and lectures. APPLY via info@abeceda.io monthly fee: 100€ More information: https://www.thenewsymposium.com/

7a2db87e7826e2ef.description: In partnership with the New York State Canal Corporation (Canal Corp.), the Erie Canal Museum (Museum) is seeking two (2) Erie Canal Artists-in-Residence (AIR) for a period of one (1) year. While all artists are encouraged to apply, we are specifically seeking artists with ancestral ties to the Haudenosaunee Confederacy and/or Mohican Nation and artists who live or work in New York State Canal communities. The Residencies will focus on a year-long creative inquiry into the New York State Canal System - including the historic Erie Canal - reflecting on its past, contemplating its current condition, and considering its future. These Residencies are for Artists who wish to engage with the Canal and adjacent Canalway Trails, Canal Corp. and Museum staff, Canal facilities, New York's Canal communities, and Canal visitors. The 2027 Residencies will be dedicated to projects that reflect upon the Canal's physical, environmental, and social condition and history; materiality; and context. The Artist's project must directly address the Canal. Applicants shall propose a specific creative visual project for their Residency that must be able to be exhibited in a gallery setting. The subject of the project shall be identified by the applicant, but proposals must be a creative inquiry of the Canal and consider a fuller, more complete account of the Canal's past, present, and future than what has traditionally been told. The applicant shall identify their target audience(s) and how their project will be shared with that audience and with the public-atlarge. While studies of Canal communities are encouraged, the Canal and its context must be central to the project. Projects may focus on key areas of the Canal or the entire system. The New York State Canal System includes 524 miles of navigable waterways and 365 of multi-use trails. Artists should consider that scale when developing their proposal. **Residency Structure:** Two (2) Artists will be selected for Residencies in 2027. The NYS Canal Corp. will facilitate introductions and connections to Canal Corp. staff and access to Canal facilities as needed. The Residency will include an exhibition of the Artists' residency work at a museum/gallery venue TBD along the Canal corridor in 2028. Artists must engage with the public. The two (2) selected Artists will participate in two (2) joint virtual panels discussing their work. One panel will be a brief introduction in early 2027 during a program concluding the 2026 Erie Canal Artist Residencies, and the second panel will be in early 2028 in a program concluding the 2027 Erie Canal Artist Residencies and introducing the 2028 Artists. Artists will also participate in a reception for their exhibition in 2028. Artists must also develop, in collaboration with the AIR partners, at least one (1) additional public-facing event during the course of the Residency for the public to engage with and understand the Artist's process. The selected artists must coordinate a visit to the Museum and a tour with the Canal Corp. prior to submitting a work plan. While a project must be proposed as part of the application, a final work plan will be required by March 1, 2027. Each Artist's final project should include work that can be displayed in a gallery setting. Artists may incorporate text and other media into their work. It is intended that final projects from the Residencies will be used to develop a joint exhibition and catalog in 2028, as well as add to the Erie Canal Museum collection. Artists must deliver their work to the exhibit site by an agreed upon date, and the exhibit will be installed by museum/gallery staff. In consultation with the Artist, project organizers will retain work(s) from the project, as well as the right to publish, with prior Artist approval, selections from the project. Throughout the Residency, the Artist, Museum, and Canal Corp., will have regular virtual or in-person check-in meetings to assist in project development. It is expected that the Residency is a part-time commitment for the Artist. **Location:** The Artists shall focus on the New York State Canal system which includes the Erie, Oswego, Cayuga-Seneca and Champlain Canals, and the Erie Canalway Trail. A workspace is not included in this Residency

7cd4b59621a48f8d.description: Open Call for Artists presents Home, an international virtual exhibition bringing together artists from around the world to explore what home means to them. Home can be familiar, distant, comforting, complicated, or constantly changing. It can be a place we know, a place we remember, a person we return to, a community we belong to, or a feeling we carry with us. Sometimes it is the home we grew up in; sometimes it is one we have left behind, built for ourselves, or continue to search for. Through this exhibition, we invite artists to look at the idea of home from their own perspective and consider the places, people, memories, experiences, and emotions that have shaped their understanding of it. The exhibition welcomes a broad range of interpretations. Your work might explore family, childhood, identity, roots, migration, belonging, culture, memory, relationships, domestic spaces, architecture, landscapes, displacement, nostalgia, or an imagined idea of home. It may be personal or universal, literal or symbolic, realistic or abstract. Home does not necessarily need to appear in the artwork itself. It can be suggested through an object, a colour, a landscape, a familiar space, a personal story, or an atmosphere that reminds us of somewhere we belong.
7cd4b59621a48f8d.title: Home

7e8010b46790195e.description: Reviving Nature 2027 International Artist Residency and Festival is now calling for applications. What if environmental action began with curiosity? What if climate conversations could be playful, creative, participatory and joyful? Reviving Nature 2027 is an international artist residency and festival exploring how art can inspire environmental awareness through play, imagination and shared experience. Rather than approaching climate change only as a crisis, we ask artists and creatives to Play • Learn • Perform • Participate: How can artists create experiences that make people care because they have participated, discovered, played and imagined together? We invite artists to transform environmental learning into an open playground where audiences become participants rather than spectators. Artists may develop interactive installations, performances, games, workshops, public interventions, storytelling, movement, sound, digital media, ecological design, socially engaged work or other interdisciplinary approaches. We are interested in work that invites people to touch, build, question, listen, move, imagine and collaborate-and, through doing so, reconnect with the living world. Projects may respond to subjects including: • climate change and environmental justice • biodiversity and ecosystems • air pollution, water and forests • food systems, waste and the circular economy • Indigenous and local knowledge • community resilience • regenerative practices • future imagination • relationships between humans and nature Projects may be poetic, experimental, educational, performative, speculative, interactive or socially engaged. The open call welcomes artists, collectives, performers, designers, researchers, educators, makers, architects, technologists, musicians, writers, filmmakers, environmental practitioners and creative thinkers from all countries. Residency period: January-March 2027 Location: Studio 88 Artist Residency, Doi Saket, Chiang Mai, Thailand
7e8010b46790195e.title: Studio 88 Artist Residency - Reviving Nature 2027 Open Call

81e9e1c5e72b0158.description: [queerphoria] is a contemporary jewelry and sculpture exhibition inviting 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals into a meaningful conversation about their identity. Through these written and visual exhibitions, we encourage dialogue around the difficult topics that surround the relationship between the queer and non-queer community. In response to global systemic dehumanization, the climate crisis, and rapid structural erosion driven by institutional power and big money, [queerphoria] returns to NYC Jewelry Week 2026 to explore the theme of restoration. Not merely as a technical process, but as a radical act of honoring queer and trans bodies, love, and evolving self-creation. [queerphoria] volume 6: restoration arrives at a critical historical time. In a landscape marked by violent legislation, AI's severe environmental and ethical impact, and destructive modern systems; the act of making by hand is inherently political. We invite makers to submit work that celebrates, mourns, deconstructs, and reimagines what restoration means within their creative practices, their movements through the world, and their personal adornment. By weaving healing together with resistance, this exhibition provides an essential narrative, reclaiming adornment as a tool to mend broken lineages, prevent erasure, and restore the fabric of our communities. [queerphoria] volume 6 builds on the previous five volumes and explores what it means to grow, evolve, and thrive as a queer artist in today's world. [queerphoria] is not only an exhibition- it is an educational platform, a cultural archive, and a radical act of visibility. Our community is an international cohort of 2SLGBTQIA+ contemporary jewelry artists, metalsmiths, and sculptors, balancing emerging makers with established voices. This year, [queerphoria] vol 6: restoration is being curated by Queer Metalsmiths' co-founder Tracey Carswell and guest jurors and [queerphoria] artists Omar Monroy and Brennan Lee.
rewards: Included artists will be showcased during NYC Jewelry Week 2026 in-person and virtually.
81e9e1c5e72b0158.title: [queerphoria] vol.6: restoration at NYC Jewelry Week

8326a4f57876e015.description: For 30 years, Fundaziun Nairs has offered an interdisciplinary, international residency program near Scuol in the Lower Engadine, Canton of Grisons. Housed in a historic bathhouse on the banks of the River Inn and surrounded by mountains, the residency brings together nine cultural practitioners and thinkers from diverse disciplines to live and work under one roof. Residencies at this former health resort - where purification and healing were once central - last between two and ten months and take place from February to November. Cooking together in the evenings is as much a part of the Fundaziun Nairs DNA as the interdisciplinary collaborations and lasting friendships formed here. In an era of increasing acceleration, fragmentation, and societal uncertainty, this location offers a rare space of possibility: a place for contemplation, concentration, and in-depth engagement with the artistic, intellectual, and societal questions of our time. Substantial artistic and intellectual processes require time - a resource that cultural practitioners here consciously grant themselves.
8326a4f57876e015.restrictions: other: Fundaziun Nairs is open to all cultural disciplines, with a focus on visual arts, performance, music, and experimental writing (including literature, scholarship, and curation). Given the linguistic diversity of the valley, we are also interested in multilingual writing practices. We strive for a dynamic social mix within the residency and encourage emerging and established practitioners of different ages, backgrounds, and disciplines to live and work here together.
8326a4f57876e015.title: Residency Fundaziun Nairs

87f5455a6935d729.description: Colloquia Futures is an annual exhibition program presented each August, dedicated to artists at the earliest stage of their professional lives. The program brings together two to three artists, typically between the ages of eighteen and twenty-five, whose work demonstrates seriousness of intent, emerging clarity, and a sustained commitment to practice. Futures is not a competition and does not operate as a survey of trends. It is a focused platform that combines early affirmation with real responsibility. Selected artists are given a fully realized exhibition within a professional gallery context, supported by curatorial dialogue, installation guidance, and rigorous presentation. The aim is not to direct an artist's development, but to create conditions in which a body of work can be articulated clearly and encountered seriously. The transition from student or self-directed practice to public exhibition is often under-supported. Futures addresses this gap by treating young artists as peers while providing structure, feedback, and care. Artists are expected to present cohesive work, consider scale and sequencing, and engage deliberately with how their work occupies space and meets an audience. The program reflects Colloquia's broader commitment to conversation as a form of cultural labor. The exhibition period includes opportunities for public discussion, informal artist conversations, and written reflection. Futures is intended to mark a moment of arrival: an early but deliberate step into sustained artistic practice. Selected artists receive a professional group exhibition, inclusion in all marketing and documentation, curatorial mentorship, and opportunities for public engagement. There are no participation fees, and Colloquia takes no commission on sales. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Artists should submit a brief statement, a small portfolio of recent work, and a short biography or résumé.
rewards: Professional exhibition, mentorship, visibility; no fees and no gallery commission on sales
87f5455a6935d729.title: Colloquia art LLC. Futures Program. 2027

92b97e2b65b08e8c.description: We are pleased to announce an open call for Legacy, the founding exhibition of our gallery program, bringing together photographers, writers, and poets whose work explores inheritance, memory, continuity, and the traces we leave behind. What is a legacy? A legacy may be something passed down by an ancestor, a predecessor, a community, or a culture. It may be a story, a tradition, a belief, a wound, a photograph, a language, or a dream for the future. Legacy asks artists and writers to reflect on what has been transmitted to them-and what they, in turn, hope to leave behind. What are you carrying from the past? What are you preserving, transforming, or challenging? What legacy are you leaving for your children, your family, your community, or the world? While our programming often engages with Africa and the African diaspora, we warmly welcome submissions from artists and writers of all backgrounds and perspectives. We Are Seeking • Photography • Photo-based projects • Poetry • Creative nonfiction • Short prose • Experimental and hybrid text works Exhibition Dates: December 16-23, 2026 Place: Neuilly-Plaisance, France Selected works will subsequently be presented at our permanent gallery space in New York during Summer of 2027. Emerging and established practitioners are encouraged to apply. 92ce1abeef23b6da.description: Amigdala is looking for three artists to take part in _Who Walks Here_, a 28-day residency at OvestLab, our civic centre in the Artisan Village, in the outskirts of Modena. **_Who Walks Here_** takes place in an Artisan Village built in 1953 by craftspeople who designed their own live-work spaces. For seventy years it has been shaped by shared labour and mutual values - but it now faces decades-long deindustrialisation and increasing real estate pressure. _Who Walks Here_ invites three artists to explore this context through a transfeminist urban lens. The construction of public space is never neutral: shaped by patriarchal logics, it produces inequalities, leaving some bodies more visible, safe and welcome than others. Places undergoing deindustrialisation are living laboratories for these questions - how can the social fabric of a neighbourhood in transformation be reimagined through care and proximity, through artistic and relational practices, rather than top-down planning? The residency continues an inquiry Amigdala opened with [_Transfemina: Intersectional Landscapes_](https://collettivoamigdala.com/portfolio-page/transfemina/), a Creative Europe project through which the collective spent two years investigating the neighbourhood and the city from a feminist perspective. Explore and create are the two inseparable movements of this process: the artists will conduct situated research on feminist urban practices in this specific context, and from that research - together with the communities who live and work here - a new site-specific piece will take shape.
open_to: Creative Europe country other than Italy

As a mobility scheme, Culture Moves Europe supports artists moving to a country different from the one they live in - so applicants based in Italy are not eligible for this call. _Who Walks Here_ is open to a wide range of practices that can meet at the intersection of performance, urban research and public space: performing arts, choreography and movement, dramaturgy, vocal and sound research, visual and public art, architecture and civic design, oral history and document

962e1bab46e37d9a.description: The Via Gluck 62 Association presents the first edition of the "BEYOND THE IMAGE ART PRIZE", an International Open Call dedicated to contemporary photography, video art, experimental film, moving images, and hybrid and installation-based practices that employ photographic and audiovisual languages. The initiative is supported by the Università Vita-Salute San Raffaele in Milan and is organized in collaboration with the University of Lausanne, StayOnBoard Art Gallery, Archivio Gabriele Basilico, and All Art Contemporary. It is promoted by the Via Gluck 62 AIR Association as part of the Milano Centrale Festival 2026. The Prize, entitled "Who Are You Beyond the Image? Art, Neuroscience and Algorithmic Narration of Experience", was established with the aim of supporting and promoting contemporary artistic research by bringing it into dialogue with the academic, scientific, and cultural worlds. Through the institutional and curatorial support of the partners involved, the Prize offers emerging and established artists a concrete exhibition opportunity, promoting projects that investigate the theme of identity in the age of digital images. THEME 2026: WHO ARE YOU BEYOND THE IMAGE? The initiative is part of the research and public engagement activities connected to the SatisFace project, dedicated to the study of the face, self-image perception, and the neuroscientific, psychological, and cultural implications of the representation of identity. The Prize aims to support works and projects that offer an original reflection on the relationship between identity, image, body perception, digital technologies, and the algorithmic narration of experience. In this first edition, the Prize is conceived as a space for interdisciplinary research dedicated to exploring the many ways in which identity is currently perceived, represented, modified, and constructed. Particular attention will be given to proposals capable of making accessible to a broad audience highly relevant scientific and cultural themes, including self-perception, facial aesthetics, the role of digital images, self-representation, visual memory, and the impact of technology on the construction of personal and collective identity. Proposals that explore the theme through photographic, audiovisual, and experimental languages, from documentary, conceptual, poetic, critical, or installation-based perspectives, are welcome. ELIGIBILITY Participation is open to artists of all nationalities. There are no age, educational, or professional experience requirements. Individual artists and collectives are eligible to apply. ELIGIBLE MEDIA Works and projects realized through the following media are eligible: • analogue and digital photography; • experimental photography; • video art; • short films; • experimental films; • audiovisual works; • video installations; • GIFs, animations, and digitally generated images; • multimedia projects integrating photography and moving images. APPLICATION PROCEDURE To apply for the Prize, applicants must complete the application form and upload the required documentation through the following link: [www.viagluck62air.com](http://www.viagluck62air.com) APPLICATION FEE The application fee is €19.00. The fee must be paid at the time of submitting the application. Via Illirico 11, 20133 Milan - Italy IBAN: IT53R0503401659000000006882 SWIFT: BAPPIT21348 The application fee contributes to the organizational and administrative costs of the Prize. 9a170cf9e10b14f6.description: **Artist Opportunity** The City of Toronto invites Canadian artists to apply for the opportunity for their work to be included as part of the custom art hoarding, to be installed along the 309-345 George Street construction. This is a two-stage competition for practicing artists who work in two-dimensional media. Priority will be given to artists that have lived experience or a connection to the Moss Park and Garden District Heritage Conservation District neighbourhood. One artist will be selected to have their work reproduced and printed on aluminum composite material (ACM) that will be installed along the construction site. The custom art hoarding will enhance the overall public environment and pedestrian streetscape experience for as long as the George Street construction is ongoing. **About the Construction Project** The George Street Revitalization (GSR) project is a transformative initiative that will replace the existing Seaton House men's shelter with a modern, purpose-built facility that integrates essential services, including a long-term care home, shelter services, supportive homes, and a community service hub. The project advances the City's commitment to addressing systemic barriers and supporting equity-deserving groups who rely on services in Toronto's Downtown East. Through a continuum of care model, the GSR will promote stability, dignity, healing, and long-term well-being while strengthening connections within the surrounding community. The project honours the site's longstanding role as a place of refuge and care. For nearly a century, beginning with Seaton House's origins in 1931 and its operation at 339 George Street from 1959, the site has provided shelter, support, and dignity to thousands of people experiencing homelessness. The redevelopment will also incorporate the historic Allan School, a designated heritage building with important connections to education, social services, and community care in the Downtown East. The Moss Park neighbourhood is situated within a broader landscape of longstanding Indigenous presence and contemporary Indigenous community-building in downtown Toronto. The area forms part of Toronto's emerging Indigenous District, with the Indigenous Centre for Innovation & Entrepreneurship at the southern end of the George Street serving as an important cultural, institutional, and economic anchor. Allan Gardens and the surrounding historic urban landscape provide an important civic context to this evolving district. Looking forward, the redevelopment of the streetscape along George Street will reflect this history through Indigenous-led placemaking, public art, planting, and gathering spaces, integrating Indigenous identity and presence into the neighbourhood's public realm. **Competition Process** An external selection panel will be convened for this competition. Four shortlisted artists will be determined based on artistic excellence and demonstrated / perceived ability to develop an engaging and site-specific public artwork. Priority will be given to artists that have lived experience or a connection to the Moss Park and Garden District Heritage Conservation District neighbourhood. Shortlisted artists will receive a Terms of Reference document to guide their next steps. Each shortlisted artist will be paid an artist fee of $1,000 to design a custom concept for the hoarding, preferably artwork that references the character and history of Moss Park and the Garden District Heritage Conservation District neighbourhood.
9a170cf9e10b14f6.restrictions: other: This is a two-stage competition for practicing artists who work in two-dimensional media. Priority will be given to artists that have lived experience or a connection to the Moss Park and Garden District Heritage Conservation District neighbourhood.
9a170cf9e10b14f6.title: George Street Construction Hoarding - Public Art Opportunity

9cb5e67d612025bb.description: FORMAT International Photography Festival is delighted to announce that in March 2027 our FORMAT27 biennale will explore the theme of PLAY. Our Open Call invites exhibition and event proposals from artists, collectives and curators across the world to respond to the festival theme with diverse and imaginative proposals. Our eminent panel of international experts, together with the FORMAT Curatorial team will review the submissions and select up to 5 projects to be exhibited at FORMAT27 in Derby between 11 March and 11 April 2027. From its first inception, the essence of photography has centered experimentation, trial and error, and exploration of something unknown; the desire to record the world around us in a way that is as close to reality as the eye can see. From Niépce's first image to the Albumen print, photogram, cyanotype and collage, the very creation of the photographic medium and its continued evolution has been developed through the act of PLAY - experimentation as play. PLAY is at the heart of the creative process, no matter the subject or idea; the act of exploration is what fuels us. FORMAT27 will seek to explore the theme in the widest possible sense, inviting people to think widely and challenge our interpretation of it. PLAY can be thought of as fun, joyful, intriguing, exploratory, experimental, challenging, deceitful, mischievous, imaginative, curious, provocative, inventive, spontaneous, subversive, engaging or perhaps rule-bending. Camera play, playing with and questioning the medium of photography itself, documenting the act of play, playing with the development of new technology, play as sport, playing with the truth or reality, the politics of play and the significance of the freedom of play being taken away are just some of the ways this broad theme could be interpreted.
9cb5e67d612025bb.restrictions: other: Entry is open to all photographers, artists, archives, collectives from anywhere in the world. We will also consider proposals for photography related events, audience participatory works, photomedia, performance, video, photobooks and archives.
9cb5e67d612025bb.title: FORMAT27 Open Call: PLAY

9d2e4a1cc3c42cbf.description: Open Call: The Difference Between Building and This one-day exhibition brings together artists who treat reference material, documents, and archives with a theatrical instinct: using them as a site to stage, build, arrange, frame, and direct. It takes up the question of what is to be done with content once it has been gathered. There is an urge here to leave the exact image behind, using reference material to create space for discourse through an object or space's unreality. "Image" is used broadly, not only the literal image commonly used as reference, but the contemporary ideal of description itself: factual, densely detailed, saturated, non-hierarchical. This condition is compounded by the sheer density of information available to artists working from reference today. With endless sources to choose from, a paradox of choice emerges, an ambivalence toward direct copy, and a desire to manipulate the image or subject instead. This sets a stage dense with contextual reference, but fertile for a point of view. As political and social discourse increasingly arrives through claims of neutrality and completeness, this exhibition is interested in artists who forgo those claims, who embrace the condition of arrangement rather than conceal it. Submitted work should construct settings in which facts, archives, and images become props within a larger theatrical arrangement, revealing the arranger's hand and how information is encountered. Please submit work concerned with: Reference Material, Archive, Staging, Theatre, Performance, Point of View, Setting, Propaganda, Rhetoric, Framing, Splicing, Translation, Material Manipulation, Assemblage, Arrangement Given the gallery's limited space, we are prioritizing a diverse range of artists and practices; not all submissions can be included. This exhibition space is provided by Flora Fauna. This show is independently organized and unaffiliated with the company.
9d2e4a1cc3c42cbf.title: Open Call: The Difference Between Building and

9e0c125d626be694.description: The Women in Arts Network is proud to present The Things We Feel, an international virtual exhibition exploring the emotions, experiences, memories, sensations, and inner worlds that shape how we experience ourselves and the world around us. Some feelings are easy to name, while others are quiet, complicated, fleeting, or difficult to put into words. This exhibition invites artists to explore the many ways feeling can become art. Your work may be inspired by a feeling, created around an emotion, shaped by a personal experience, connected to a memory, or simply evoke a feeling in the viewer. The theme is intentionally open to interpretation. Artists may explore love, grief, joy, longing, fear, nostalgia, belonging, vulnerability, desire, solitude, hope, connection, transformation, or any other feeling or experience that has found its way into their creative practice. Designed for artists working across all visual mediums, this opportunity brings together a diverse selection of works from artists around the world, creating a visual conversation around the deeply human experiences that connect us all. Selected artists will be featured in an international virtual exhibition hosted by the Women in Arts Network. Presented through an online gallery, the exhibition will be accessible worldwide, allowing artists to share their work with collectors, curators, fellow artists, art enthusiasts, and audiences across the globe.

Your space is not guaranteed until payment-or the first installment of a payment plan-is received. ​ Payment plans are available at adjusted rates for applicants who prefer to pay in installments. ​ Refund Policy All fees and installments are 100% nonrefundable. This includes withdrawal, schedule conflicts, emergencies, travel issues, or inability to attend the in‐person graduation ceremony.
