ac60dbebc9efe92f.description: Located on the sixth floor of the Museum and open to the public, the Artist Studios at MAD is a community engagement and professional development program for contemporary artists and designers. The first museum residency of its kind, the program encourages visitor engagement with Artist Studios Residents as they expand their creative practice while working on site at MAD. Two artists are selected for six-month sessions (August-February or February-August), for which they receive access to studio space in the Museum and a stipend. Open studio hours are held Wednesday 11 am to 7 pm, and Thursday through Saturday from 10:30 am to 5:30 pm. During that time, the artists welcome Museum visitors inside their workspaces for conversation and close looking. The artists chosen for MAD's Artist Studios program represent a wide range of creative practices within the fields of art, craft, and design. Established in 2008, the program has served as an important platform for more than 200 artists and designers to advance their careers and is widely recognized as an innovative model for Museum education. Alumni have gone on to highly regarded careers and have exhibited at MAD and other major institutions, including the Queens Museum, Whitney Museum, Brooklyn Museum, and Studio Museum, among others. **Residency Expectations** Artist Studios Residents commit to 14 or 21 public open studio hours per week on Thursdays, Fridays, and/or Saturdays from 10:30 am to 5:30 pm and/or Wednesdays 11:00 am to 7:00 pm. The daily residents' weekly schedule will be established in conjunction with MAD's Education Department and will remain set throughout the six-month residency. In addition to their public open studio hours during each assigned week in the Museum, Artist Studios Residents are encouraged to utilize the studio space for private studio hours. During their weekly open studio hours, all Artist Studios residents will welcome visits from K-12 school groups facilitated by paid artist-educators and public tour groups by docents. The Artist Studios program offers three residencies per six-month session. Starting Friday, August 14, MAD is accepting applications for the **February 15, 2027- August 15, 2027 (Cycle 46)** or and **August 16, 2027- February 13, 20278 (Cycle 47)** Artists will be selected to participate in one session and will mark which session(s) they are applying for within the application.

b37c44c0c3c5aa96.description: Can art bend the future? We're excited to open applications for the 2026 Ping-Pong Residency in Berlin. Ping-Pong Between Art and Knowledge invites applications from artists, writers, thinkers, and cultural workers whose practices explore how art can shape the way we imagine what is to come. We ask whether art has the power to change how we think about the future, to shift the ways we perceive it, and to reframe the forms of communication through which we share these visions. The residency offers a dedicated space in the center of Berlin for concentrated exploration, reflection, and dialogue across art, philosophy, and science. It is a place to slow down, to test ideas, and to open questions that are not easily answered. We are particularly interested in projects that look closely at the role of technology, not simply as a practical tool, but as a force that merges with artistic thinking and imagination. In this light, we welcome work that engages with technology as both a material and a cultural condition: one that can generate new ways of sensing, knowing, and speculating about possible futures. Rather than seeking finished works or definitive answers, we value processes that remain open, exploratory, and experimental. We encourage projects that challenge familiar perspectives, unsettle assumptions, and expand our collective vocabulary for thinking and talking about what lies ahead. The residency is not about predicting the future, it is about creating new ways to approach it, to imagine it, and perhaps even to bend it. Since 2018, Ping-Pong has hosted internationally recognised artists and emerging voices alike, always with an eye toward projects that connect art, technology, and society in unexpected ways. We look forward to welcoming the next group of residents into this growing network of curious, inventive people who believe art can help shape a liveable future.
b37c44c0c3c5aa96.title: 2026 Micro Residency Program in the Heart of Berlin

b455f7a363ac3ef3.description: A fellowship year at Harvard Radcliffe Institute is an opportunity to step away from usual routines and dive deeply into a project in a uniquely interdisciplinary and creative community. Radcliffe supports engaged scholarship, through which fellows develop new tools and methods, challenge artistic and scholarly conventions, and shed light on our past and our present. **Community** In the private offices and artist studios of Byerly Hall, fellows have dedicated time and space to pursue their projects alongside scientists, writers, scholars, public intellectuals, and artists whose work is shaping their fields and the wider world. Whether gathering in common areas around the Institute, sitting under the apple tree in Radcliffe Yard, or meeting over lunch, fellows regularly come together to share insights and build connections. Each week, two fellows present their work in progress either in a private talk for their cohort or in a public lecture, forming the foundation of the program's interdisciplinary community. Group lunches follow each talk, providing a forum for deeper conversation and feedback. Fellowship socials and outings are held throughout the year for fellows and their families to explore the Cambridge/Boston area. **Professional Development** While in residence, fellows enjoy access to Harvard Library's system, including the Schlesinger Library and its rich collections. Fellowship Program staff facilitate other opportunities, including professional development workshops, events with Radcliffe faculty directors, and the opportunity to work with Harvard College undergraduates as research partners. In the Radcliffe Research Partnership Program, Harvard undergraduate students intellectually engage with fellows and their projects by providing research assistance, reviewing book chapters, discussing new approaches to projects, and more.

bb3e7df58916c2dd.description: The images that circulate globally play a powerful role in shaping how gender, power, and social realities are understood - influencing everything from public debate and cultural memory to research, advocacy, and policy. Yet the communities, cultural contexts, and visual practices that should inform these narratives too often remain underrepresented in the images and institutions that influence them. The Regional Curatorial Fellows Programme exists to help shift that. For the first time, This is Gender is embedding regional curators directly within the heart of its global photography competition - bringing local knowledge, critical perspective, and lived context into how work is discovered, interpreted, contextualised, and shared. This is an opportunity to help reshape the platform from within - influencing not only which images are seen, but how gender is framed, debated, and acted upon across cultural, public, and policy spaces.
bb3e7df58916c2dd.restrictions: other: Applications are welcomed from: * Curators * Critics and writers * Researchers * Artistic directors * Photographers * Organisers * Cultural practitioners Applicants should come from global majority countries or historically underrepresented communities, including those across Asia, Africa, Latin America, the Middle East, Oceania, and diasporic communities worldwide. Early-career practitioners and recent graduates are particularly encouraged to apply. Applicants do not need to hold a formal curatorial job title.
bb3e7df58916c2dd.title: This is Gender: Regional Curatorial Fellowship

be14357fcab42f91.description: We are a multi-racial, multi-ethnic, multi-generational cooperative of creatives, educators, and farmers with a common mission to create a community based on shared values and democratic principles. We believe in sustainable living through regenerative agriculture, community outreach, education, and inclusivity. We are stewarding 66 acres of wooded mountainside with trails, forest, fields, and streams in the lush green mountains in Fletcher, Vermont. Join us to begin conversations around social, racial, and environmental justice and the role we, as artist/educators/activists, play in uplifting the next generation of artist/activist leaders! We have beautiful outdoor spaces for plein air painting, abundant woods for crafting and sculpting with natural materials, and woods to explore for inspiration and contemplation. Bring your sustainable art supplies, small tools, sketchbooks, and wisdom, to make art, grow food, and be the change we want to see in the world! Guests are invited to stay on the property, participate in building projects on the land, and contribute to conversations about how we can build a sustainable, equitable place for BIPOC, ALAANA, and LGBTQIA+ creative communities + culture workers. We offer short term (1 week -4 weeks) and long term (6 week - 8 week) residencies. Depending on the season, you may stay in the Kindred House, the Kindred Cottage, Yurt, three season tents, tent platform, or camp in the field. Our residency is meant to inspire you, offer a place to rest, and support creativity surrounded by nature. Artists, writers, think-tanks, educators and learners, farmers and community activists, and culture workers are invited to apply. Please contact us to find out how our creative residence may contribute to your goals.

The fellowship requires a 9-month commitment, based on a mutually agreed-upon work plan. Applicants must be at least 21 years of age and eligible to work legally in the United States. c4f4484717dd3d47.description: DiversaMente Art Curator Magazine invites artists from all countries and artistic disciplines to participate in Issue 3 - October 2026. Each issue reaches an international audience of more than 150,000 readers, with readership continuing to grow. The magazine is followed by artists, collectors, curators, galleries and cultural professionals, and reaches libraries, universities and cultural institutions worldwide. Its international circulation also makes the publication accessible to readers through hospitality and travel environments, including hotels, airlines and cruise ships. The opportunity is open to visual artists, painters, sculptors, photographers, digital and mixed-media artists, illustrators, performers, theatre and dance professionals, musicians and practitioners from other artistic disciplines. Participating artists are presented through a dedicated editorial space designed to introduce their work, artistic research and professional identity to an international readership. Depending on the chosen editorial format, the publication may include artworks, technical details, biographical information, professional contacts and a critical text signed by the Editorial Direction. DiversaMente Art Curator Magazine is conceived as a meeting point between contemporary artistic practice and an international audience interested in discovering artists, projects and new creative research. Deadline: 23 October 2026.
rewards: Two-page Artist Focus - two facing editorial pages dedicated to the artist, including artworks, tech

c51ed4d5f6191708.description: With its unparalleled reach, the Sony World Photography Awards elevate the careers of photographers to the next level. Produced by Creo under its photography strand, the World Photography Organisation, the Sony World Photography Awards has been running since 2007 and is widely regarded as one of the leading international photography competitions. c762d2fa570986a4.description: On 7 June 2026, the 12th International Awards for Art Criticism (IAAC 12) was officially launched at the Sichuan Fine Arts Institute, inviting submissions of art reviews in Chinese or English from around the globe. IAAC 12 is jointly run by the IAAC Organising Committee, the School of Philosophy at Fudan University, and the Shanghai Zhangyuan Art Museum (in preparation), with support from the Royal College of Art in London, the Edinburgh College of Art and the International Association of Art Critics (AICA). The IAAC 12 international jury comprises five members: * Fiona Bradley, Director, Fruitmarket, Edinburgh. * Ben Eastham, art critic and novelist based in London. He is the editor-in-chief of e-flux Criticism. * Richard J. Williams, Professor of Contemporary Visual Cultures at the University of Edinburgh. * WANG Pu, Associate Professor of Chinese Literature and Culture and Chair of the Department of German, Russian and Asian Languages and Literature, Brandeis University. * XIANG Zairong, Associate Professor of Comparative Literature and Director of Arts at Duke Kunshan University The Organising Committee of the International Awards for Art Criticism aims to support independent critical coverage of contemporary art, away from the immediate pressures of the market, media and private patronage. The Awards are to stimulate good writing, critical thinking and dialogue and research in China, the UK and wider afield. The objectivity of the selection process is underpinned, both by the recognised professionalism of the Chinese and English-speaking jury members and by the strict anonymity of the judging process.
c762d2fa570986a4.restrictions: other: **The Twelfth Edition is open to candidates from anywhere in the world writing in Chinese or English about any contemporary art exhibition held anywhere in the world or on-line between 1 September 2025 and 31 August 2026.** Candidates are invited to write a review of 1,500 English words or 2,500 Chinese characters on any exhibition of contemporary art. The submissions shall not previously have been published anywhere else.
c762d2fa570986a4.title: 12th International Awards for Art Criticism

Numèric 2026 is a collaboration between Les antípodes and Bòlit, Centre d'Art Contemporani, Girona, and the Museu de l'Empordà, Figueres, with the support of the Generalitat de Catalunya, Agullana Town Council, Figueres Town Council and Acción Cultural Española (AC/E) through the PICE - Residencias nacionales programme.

c8b840ab017e3af8.description: BE OPEN ArtLimitless is an international open call celebrating creative approaches to sustainability, reuse and circular thinking. The initiative invites artists, designers, sculptors, architects and other creative practitioners to submit works and projects that explore how existing materials and resources can be given a new life. Eligible approaches may include recycling, upcycling, repurposing, the use of reclaimed or reused materials, low-waste processes, material experimentation and other forms of environmentally conscious art-making. Submissions may take a wide range of forms, including visual art, sculpture, installation, mixed media, craft, textile and fibre art, photography, digital and new media art, product or industrial design, sustainable design, architecture, public art and interdisciplinary practice. Participation is free and open to applicants worldwide. The call is intended for creative practitioners whose work engages meaningfully with sustainability, materials, environmental responsibility or circularity. Submitted projects should be original and clearly presented through images and a short description explaining the concept, materials and creative process. Selected works will be featured on the BE OPEN Art online platform and may be promoted through the Foundation's communications. Participants will also be considered for three monetary awards: • €1,000 Jury Prize • €500 Founder's Choice Prize • €300 Public Vote Prize BE OPEN ArtLimitless aims to support artists and designers who demonstrate that creativity can transform discarded, overlooked or existing resources into meaningful new work, while encouraging wider reflection on more sustainable ways of living and making.
rewards: • €1,000 Jury Prize • €500 Founder's Choice Prize • €300 Public Vote Prize
c8b840ab017e3af8.title: BE OPEN ArtLimitless

caa336f06accf000.description: Zad is a support framework designed to promote mobility and communication for artists from the Arab region residing in Europe. Its main objective is to develop their artistic and professional path in collaboration with their peers and across various artistic spaces and platforms. Additionally, Zad assists artists in reaching and engaging with different types of audiences, all while enhancing their contributions to public life within the cities and countries in which they reside and work. Zad's support covers all artistic and literary specialisations and is open to individuals of all ages. Some examples of this support include: presenting theatrical works and live artistic performances, concerts at music festivals, streaming films in cities and places where they have not previously been streamed, organising or joining literary readings, organising and relocating art exhibitions, and sharing the outcomes of artist residencies.
caa336f06accf000.restrictions: other: All artists (individuals or groups) from the Arab region, regardless of their ethnic background, who have relocated to Europe since 2015, are eligible to apply. The programme gives priority to artists who moved from the following countries: Syria, Palestine, Lebanon, Iraq, Jordan, Egypt, Yemen, Sudan, and Libya.

cc9c9f9fb56afbe1.description: For the **_WRG Digital Call-Out: Generation Xi_**, applicants are invited to create an artwork inspired by the aesthetic of _New Ugly_. _New Ugly_ is a design movement that gleefully discards traditional rules of composition, embracing chaos, imperfection, and visual excess. It celebrates the awkward, the unconventional, and the deliberately disruptive. The result is a bold visual language that resonates with a generation raised in an era of information overload, algorithmic feeds, and constant digital stimulation. _New Ugly_ is not about poor design-it is about intentionally challenging established conventions to create something fresh, expressive, and distinctly contemporary.

cffd4e6c42cd6a25.description: Fondazione Pistoletto Cittadellarte and UNIDEE Residency Programs, in collaboration with UniCredit Group, announce the third edition of [the open call "Ecosystems as Living Communities"](https://unidee.cittadellarte.it/activity.html?id=263), supporting two production residencies for emerging international artists working with socially engaged artistic practices that address contemporary ecological issues. The third edition, continuing under the theme "Ecosystems as Living Communities", invites artists to further explore global, contemporary, and future ecological challenges, fostering positive and regenerative visions of desirable futures. Artists are encouraged to propose projects that investigate ecosystems as interconnected communities of humans and non-humans, challenging anthropocentric perspectives and promoting an ecocentric mindset. Two selected artists will engage in a shared research phase, including meetings with tutors, researchers, and experts, as well as field visits. The residency structure and schedule will be tailored to each project and defined collaboratively with the artists. A collaborative attitude and flexibility in developing and implementing the projects-consistent with the evolving research process-are therefore essential. The resulting works will be publicly presented at Cittadellarte in Biella and will become part of the UniCredit Art Collection. Moreover, the outcomes of the residencies will be disseminated online, contributing to broader public awareness and promoting responsible engagement with ecological and social transformation.
cffd4e6c42cd6a25.restrictions: other: \- The production residencies are open to emerging and mid-career artists, designers, architects, fashion designers, musicians, filmmakers, and other cultural practitioners whose creative practices engage with contemporary ecological issues. \- Applications are welcome from practitioners working across all disciplines, media, and methodologies, provided they can demonstrate previous experience in the production of artistic works. Interdisciplinary, cross-disciplinary, and experimental approaches are encouraged. **\- Two artists will be selected: one Italian artist and one international
cffd4e6c42cd6a25.title: "Ecosystems as Living Communities" vol. III

d02b0aa2319c9c97.description: The Más Retina Association organizes and announces the **6th BARCELONA HUMAN RIGHTS AND GLOBAL JUSTICE PHOTOGRAPHY AWARD**. The Festival will consist of 10 large-format exhibitions selected from through this open call. These exhibitions will be displayed in public spaces, on the streets of Barcelona-one in each district-**from December 1, 2026, to January 10, 2027.** **BCN-DH International Photo Festival** seeks to shed light on global issues and their root causes using photography as a tool to advance social justice, environmental sustainability, and the exercise of all rights within the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). d21cc780a4132e20.description: **This year's PhotoVogue Global Open Call embraces creativity as rebellion, inviting photographers and video makers to use image-making to challenge indifference, disrupt conventions, and expand visual storytelling.** This open call does not ask for a theme to illustrate. **It asks for a position**. It asks for a position in relation to the world as it is. In relation to what one refuses. In relation to what one longs for, questions, resists, imagines, or defends. There is no single answer. It may take the form of intimacy, care, or attention. It may take the form of confrontation, rupture, or refusal. It may involve invention, disobedience, new visual languages, new aesthetics, and the imagining of new worlds. What matters is not whether the work belongs to fashion, art, documentary, photography, or video. What matters is the force, the urgency, and the necessity behind it. To create in this context also means allowing oneself a deeper freedom. A freedom from repetition. A freedom from expectation. A freedom from approval. It means creating without the need to please. At a time when so much is made to disappear into the stream, this open call is an invitation to resist that disappearance. Create from urgency, not habit. Create from conviction, not compliance. Do not illustrate the world as it is. **Answer it.**

This can take many forms, from powerful storytelling to images that stand out for their aesthetic impact. ❌ **AI-generated works are not eligible.**

d5c37e0861b43dff.description: The Art in Public Places Program of New Mexico Arts at the NM Department of Cultural Affairs (NMDCA), in collaboration with Spaceport America seek an artist/artist team to create a public art sundial - a functional work of art. The sundial artwork will be installed outside the newly built STARC (Spaceport Technology and Reception Center) at Spaceport America, an earthbound but aspirational space dedicated to inquiry in the high desert southwest of New Mexico. The intent of the sundial is to creatively represent the origins of measurement and human curiosity. At its essence, a sundial is a chronometric device that translates Earth's rotation into a visual, accurate representation of time. By intercepting the sun's rays, it uses the position and length of a shadow to indicate the hour, essentially serving as a bridge between celestial mechanics and terrestrial life. Sundials are at least 3,500 years old. In this installation, the sundial acts as a functional work of art, reminding us that time is not merely a digital abstraction but a physical consequence of humanity's journey through the solar system. It connects the cosmos, the blue sky, the sun, and the vast, beautiful Jornada de Muerto basin to the mechanical and tactile realism of Spaceport America. It should evoke curiosity and wonder. A sundial is the ancestor of the clock, the calendar, and the computer. It is one of humankind's first attempts to understand the universe. People in New Mexico, no matter who they are or when they live, have always honored the workings of the cosmos. * Interactivity: More than just a work of art, a sundial invites the observer to engage with the environment and with time itself. It highlights the changing seasons through the shifting length of the shadow - long and sweeping in winter, short and sharp in summer. It should spark curiosity about cosmic motions. * Symbolism: It stands as a monument to constancy. While technology evolves, the relationship between the sun and the Earth remains the most reliable metronome in human history. A sundial attests to both the motion of the Earth in relation to the sun and the consistency of that motion over the centuries. * Artistry: The artist/artist team has the choice of evoking other feelings and emotions about time, space, technology, the vast desert and sky, and the human condition, as we reach for the stars at New Mexico's Spaceport. A sundial consists of two fundamental components that work in tandem: 1. The Gnomon: Derived from the Greek word for "one who knows," the gnomon is the vertical or angled element that casts the shadow. In a scientifically accurate installation, the gnomon's angle is typically set to the latitude of its location, aligning it parallel to the Earth's axis of rotation. 2. The Dial Plate: The surface onto which the shadow is cast. This plate is inscribed with hour lines and, often, seasonal markets. As the sun moves across the sky from east to west, the shadow moves across the plate in the opposite direction. During the peak of the sun's arc, the sundial will indicate the solar noon. Artists may interpret these elements as they see fit to fulfill their artistic vision, while maintaining the elements that would keep this artwork a functioning sundial. The intent of this open competition is to select finalists that demonstrate highly unique and creative expressions of historical and/or scientific objects and their functions, while evoking a sense of wonder by the viewer. The high desert open landscape invites experimental but functional approaches to this important object of measurement.
d5c37e0861b43dff.restrictions: other: This REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS is open to all artists/artist teams currently residing in the United States. Artists submitting qualifications should demonstrate a level of experience and professionalism that is commensurate with the project scope and budget.
d5c37e0861b43dff.title: Spaceport America Sundial Public Art Project

efaa2386890c8cbf.description: For our upcoming issue, we are looking for **drawings** that approach the city in all its forms: as a place, a system, a social structure, an organism, a memory or an idea. It might appear through maps, public space, housing, transport, migration, displacement, urban nature, borders, crowds, solitude or everyday life. It may be real, remembered, imagined, invented or yet to come. Cities are never fixed. They are constantly built, transformed, expanded, neglected and remade. Shaped by architecture and infrastructure as much as by movement, politics, ecology and the people who inhabit them, they carry traces of the past while continually making room for possible futures. Cities bring different lives into proximity. People meet, pass one another, share spaces, remain strangers or build communities. Neighbourhoods evolve, buildings disappear and new structures emerge. The visible city is only one layer of a larger network of relationships, histories and invisible systems.
efaa2386890c8cbf.restrictions: other: We welcome a broad range of approaches and interpretations. Drawing can observe, document, analyse, question, speculate or reinvent the urban world. It can focus on the visible fabric of the city or reveal the forces, tensions and hidden structures that shape it.
efaa2386890c8cbf.title: OPEN CALL FUKT #24 - THE CITY ISSUE

f0625211cebbffbc.description: Il progetto, indetto da La Fondazione Le Stanze Della Fotografia e dall'Associazione per il Patrimonio delle Colline del Prosecco di Conegliano e Valdobbiadene, prevede il lancio di un concorso gratuito e aperto a tutti, finalizzato alla raccolta di testimonianze, racconti e suggestioni legate al tema dell'acqua all'interno dei patrimoni culturali e paesaggistici. L'iniziativa nasce con l'obiettivo di valorizzare la memoria, la cultura e le tradizioni dei territori, offrendo uno spazio di espressione e narrazione aperto a cittadini, studenti, fotografi, videomaker e appassionati di storytelling. Il progetto prende avvio dalle Colline del Prosecco di Conegliano e Valdobbiadene, Patrimonio dell'Umanità UNESCO, ma si apre a uno sguardo più ampio, invitando i partecipanti a esplorare il tema anche in relazione ad altri patrimoni dell'umanità, in Italia e nel mondo. L'acqua diventa così un filo narrativo universale, capace di collegare luoghi, culture e comunità attraverso immagini, parole e racconti visivi. L'edizione inaugurale del concorso è dedicata all'elemento acqua, intesa nelle sue molteplici forme e significati: l'acqua che scorre nei paesaggi naturali, che irriga e sostiene l'agricoltura, l'acqua rappresentata nell'arte e nella cultura, l'acqua come risorsa simbolica. I partecipanti saranno invitati a raccontare questo elemento attraverso fotografia, scrittura e video, costruendo narrazioni che uniscano dimensione visiva e riflessione personale.
rewards: I progetti selezionati avranno l'opportunità di essere esposti presso le Stanze della Fotografia.
f0625211cebbffbc.title: Open Call Immagini e trame d'acqua.

f0f55d529f1ab1f0.description: Leica Society International (LSI) is proud to announce its tenth annual _Photography Grant_. We are looking for work in still-images that create space for people, places, communities, histories, or issues to be witnessed with care, dignity, and intention. **Strong submissions should show:** * Who or what is being seen * What has kept this story unseen, unseen clearly, or misrepresented * What changes when the subject is witnessed with care * How the photographer creates trust, presence, and respect through the work * What the images reveal about dignity, identity, agency, or belonging * At its core, this theme asks: What becomes possible when a person, story, or community is truly seen.

Across its previous nine editions, more than 90 artists from around the world have been selected, forming an international community working across a wide range of artistic languages, methodologies and contemporary concerns. Many former participants have subsequently exhibited in museums, institutions, galleries and international projects, while several have gone on to become represented artists of GALERIA REUS. The gallery may also select one of the participating artists or collectives for a solo exhibition within one year of the group exhibition's closing. Applications must be submitted as one single PDF portfolio including an updated CV, artist statement, available and unpublished works, contact details and any additional relevant information.
